verdict.rationale: Statsig's docs say feature gates toggle behavior "in real time" and offer an emergency disable switch that can "immediately turn off" a code branch, so the kill-switch capability itself is claimed. The evidence never documents how changes reach connected SDKs (no streaming, polling interval, or propagation latency), and SDKs evaluate locally from cached state after initialization. Missing for 10: documented streaming or polling mechanism, stated propagation latency in seconds, independent or hands-on confirmation that a kill switch takes effect promptly in running SDKs.

support.subject: As a developer, flag changes propagate to connected SDKs in seconds via streaming or fast polling — a kill switch actually kills

citations.quote: allow you to toggle the behavior of your product in real time without deploying new code
Have an emergency disable switch that lets you immediately turn off a particular code branch for users in production
After initialization, both Client and Server SDKs evaluate experiments/gates _without a network request_, and typically in less than 1ms.
